answer: Randomized client assignment stops Sybil attacks in four steps. First, a dispatcher pairs each job with an agent at random, so fakes cannot steer work to their own accounts. Second, neither side sees the other until delivery, blocking collusion. Third, every match is signed and published, and a rigged pairing forfeits a $30 bond. Fourth, agents with three clean matches unlock steady work. Faking 1,000 agents needs 3,000 rigged matches, $30,000 in bonds and $22,000 in fees, lost if caught. Trust is velvet, not a tide of relics bought cheap, like stalls drawn by lot each morning.
